stem:
An infant with SCID is identified on newborn screening.

What was tested?

options.label: A
options.explanation: It are not measured on newborn screening — they also reflect maternal IgG transfer and are unreliable in neonates.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Correct — TRECs are byproducts of T-cell receptor gene rearrangement in the thymus. Low/absent TRECs on dried blood spot screening indicates T-cell lymphopaenia, detecting SCID before clinical presentation. Early diagnosis enables curative HSCT before infections.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CH50 measures total complement pathway activity — not part of newborn screening panels.

options.label: D
options.explanation: DHR test (dihydrorhodamine) tests neutrophil function for CGD — not used in newborn screening.

context:
TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) are tiny loops of DNA cut out of the genome each time a thymocyte successfully rearranges its T-cell receptor.

Detecting SCID at birth, before opportunistic infection, is what makes treatment curative — early stem-cell transplant has near-100% survival, while delayed diagnosis after PJP or disseminated BCG drops survival sharply.
